name: The History Series
short_description: Reimagines cultural narratives by laying memes, cartoons, and historical figures over art-historical references — a meditation on what happens to history in the age of hyperlinks.
full_description: In the history series I explore the construction of disparate narratives and the clashes between these constructions as they come together in the real world. This evokes feelings of alienation, juxtaposition, and original significance, creating parallels between cartoons and the flattened schizophrenic subjectivities in these paintings. My characters are layered memes and archetypes from art history and popular culture. The series uncovers a space of alienation in which the production of totalities can be subverted, where the textbook narrative, the comic book narrative, and the meme going viral all collide. Images from Picasso's Guernica, Manet's Olympia, and Garafolo's Annunciation are unraveled and incorporated into a personal story of interaction with these images. Daffy Duck and other characters inhabit the paintings as invitations — familiar in both imagery and circumstance — and the moment of judgment is part of a commitment to collaborative storytelling.

name: Impossible Bouquets
short_description: Inspired by the Dutch still-life tradition of impossible bouquets — flowers from different seasons made to coexist on canvas. A metaphor for being Indian: an impossible democracy, an impossible bouquet.
full_description: The Impossible Bouquet Series is inspired by the Dutch tradition of still life where flowers are collected from different seasons to create an Impossible Bouquet. What I found fascinating was that these flowers can never coexist — they belong to different seasons. However, in this particular arrangement they come together beautifully. Not very different from the condition of our minds, where impossible concepts coexist to create our spirit and our sense of being. For me, this is the condition of being Indian — an impossible democracy, an impossible bouquet. A space where seemingly conflicting entities like cartoons, memes, historical characters coexist, creating a harmonious impossible sense of beauty. I see everything as an integrated interactive storytelling experience. Guernica meets the traditional masks of Bali within a video game culture. Politics, pragmatism, ideologies, beauty, gradients all come together to create this Impossible Bouquet which I celebrate through my paintings.

name: The Guernica Project
short_description: A decade-long dialogue with Picasso's Guernica, reframing its external war through an Indian philosophical lens — internal conflict, ghosts of partition, the wars within.
full_description: Picasso's Guernica haunted me for years. Its jagged chaos captured the horrors of war with a universality that feels timeless. Standing before it, I began to feel something else stirring — questions not just about the wars outside, but about the wars within. What would it mean to take Picasso's vision and respond to it, not as an observer of history but as someone grappling with the inner conflicts that shape us all? In this series I overlay a post-colonial reality on a Western narrative, arriving at a kind of post-modernism after the fact — one that uses savage irony and gallows humor to dislocate its predecessor's emphasis on pastiche, whimsy, and play. The Holocaust was, in a sense, the death of the Western imagination; the Partition was another holocaust, not even named as such, silenced, papered over. Reinscribing the trauma of the Partition onto Guernica requires a different mood, a dislocated universe. Gandhi, Nehru, Jinnah appear as Ravana, as the octo-mom, as dragons — mirroring the various uses, misuses, reuses, and abuses these specters of the past have been put to in contemporary Indian discourse. Mutant gods hobnob with Disney cartoons. The Hindu cultural colonialism in Bali makes a surprise appearance. Amidst the confusion is a circle of peace where the eye rests, flanked by the Owl of Athena and the Swan of Brahma — emblems of wisdom, Western and Indian. What will occupy this space? Hope, but a blank hope, ready to be written over by the future. The 2022 Volte Art Projects exhibition in Dubai (Guernica Reimagined) extended the work into digital prints and 69 NFTs, opening during the early days of the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

name: Sublime Machines
short_description: Imagines scientific reality as a source of the sublime. A compositional process that is part human, part algorithm, translating digital tools into acrylic on canvas.
full_description: In this series of artworks, Sublime Machines, I imagine scientific reality as a new source of the sublime. Historically, the sublime has been tied to the awe-inspiring forces of nature; in our contemporary era, scientific exploration and digital innovation occupy that space. I reinvest the often detached, clinical sphere of science with human emotion and intent, pushing the boundaries of how we interpret and experience technology through art. I sought to refigure the notions of transcendence and sublimity for our time and its future. To achieve this, I developed a new compositional process that is both human and algorithm-driven. By blending digital modes of creation — procedural drawing tools, vector brushes, gradient fills — with traditional material realities like acrylic on canvas, I wanted to challenge the dichotomy between the immaterial precision of the digital and the tactile resonance of the physical. This body of work is a meditation on how technological tools, often seen as utilitarian, can be imbued with emotional depth, becoming collaborators in creative expression.

name: The Orgasm Project
short_description: La Petite Mort. EEG-recorded orgasm translated into 3D digital model and robotically-painted canvas — a critique of commodifying human intimacy in the NFT era.
full_description: In 2021, through La Petite Mort, I transformed one of humanity's most intimate experiences — an orgasm — into a work of art bridging neuroscience, AI, and robotics. Using EEG technology developed with neuroscientist Abhijeet Satani, I recorded my brain waves during orgasm. The neural patterns were transformed into a 3D digital model by Harshit Agrawal, then translated by Artmatr's robotic painting technology into large-scale 74×74 canvases. The project asks: if everything in the world can be digitized, where do our boundaries lie? In a time when social media has turned half the population into performers and the other half into spectators, what happens when we can consume each other's most personal, intimate experiences? By tokenizing my own orgasm and selling it as art at Sotheby's x Burning Man Online Auction, I invite audiences to confront an uncomfortable future where nothing, not even our deepest moments of intimacy, is off-limits. The French call the orgasm la petite mort — 'the little death' — and for me, it represents both an end and a beginning, a moment where the mental and physical collapse into one.

name: Edges
short_description: Nine 2020 oil-on-canvas works (including two diptychs) posing existential questions about the body, identity, and the boundaries between self and other.

name: Mysterium, Tremendum et Fascinans
short_description: Robotic-assisted paintings made with Artmatr's X1, X2, and Sozo. A series about identity collapse and renewal, drawing on Rudolf Otto's notion of the numinous.
full_description: When I embarked on creating Mysterium, Tremendum et Fascinans (MTF), I was navigating one of the most tumultuous periods of my personal and artistic journey. This series is born out of my desire to infuse human intent into algorithms and geometries, crafting new forms of transcendent experiences that resonate with our current digital anthropocene. MTF is a reflection of my evolving understanding of self and identity, influenced profoundly by the unraveling of a 17-year relationship. Collaborating with my brother Karthik, we delved into the essence of transcendence, borrowing from Rudolf Otto's definition of the numinous as mysterium tremendum et fascinans — an attractive yet awe-inspiring mystery. We identified three core elements essential to any transcendent experience: liberation, the loss of identity, and the comfort within mystery. The project utilizes three robots — X1, X2, and Sozo — from Artmatr Labs to augment my creative process. Each piece is a unique dialogue between my emotional state and the machine's capabilities, capturing the fragmented and evolving nature of memory and identity. Every time I recreate a work, I am not merely recalling a memory but reshaping it, highlighting the interplay between the digital and the real. Exhibited at Artmatr Gallery in Chelsea, New York City, 2018.

name: Eye Candy
short_description: Performance art on Instagram (2020-2021): seven emotions explored through Side A / Side B / Play. The physical canvases are the residue of a digital-first show.
full_description: When the world came to a standstill in 2020, I began to question the relevance of art in a world overwhelmed by chaos. Traditional galleries felt inaccessible, yet the need for connection had never been more urgent. If art was to reach people where they were, it needed to meet them on the screens we were all glued to. Collaborating with Anto Philip and Under25 Studios, I launched Eye Candy — a performance art project that reimagined the possibilities of digital storytelling. The project explores seven emotions: love, loss, boundaries, truth, balance, introspection, and perspective. Each emotion is expressed through three conceptual layers: Side A (one perspective), Side B (its counterpoint), and Play (the space where resolution emerges). Using Instagram's native tools — Reels, Carousels, IGTV videos, Lives — I sought to create a hybrid exhibition that felt organic to the medium while maintaining the depth of traditional art. The physical canvases catalogued here are the studio companions to that digital body of work, crossing 100,000 views across seven episodes.

name: The Figure Series

name: The Impossible Bouquet 2.0
short_description: AI-driven artworks exploring human-machine collaboration. Acrylic + digital print on archival cotton rag. Exhibited at 24 Jor Bagh, The Gujral Foundation, Feb 2023.
full_description: When I first encountered the world of AI image generation, I was filled with equal parts curiosity and anxiety. As an artist who has spent decades exploring human vulnerability and creativity, the idea of collaborating with something bodiless, something non-human, was both thrilling and unnerving. The Impossible Bouquet 2.0 grew out of my attempt to navigate this tension — a playful and deeply personal dialogue with a technology that is reshaping the creative landscape. The project is inspired by the Dutch still-life tradition of 'impossible bouquets,' where flowers from different seasons — plants that could never coexist in nature — are painted together in harmonious arrangements. To me, this concept mirrors the strange and wondrous possibilities of collaborating with AI. Initial prompts were fed into image-generating AI to produce provocative juxtapositions: bouquets made of recycled plastic, food, human anatomy, hand-blown glass fused with metal. Dissatisfied with the AI's flatness, I reclaimed control by painting over the digitally printed images, blending my artistic vision with the machine's contributions. AI doesn't judge. It doesn't flinch at intimacy or strangeness. This made the collaboration deeply liberating — I could feed it prompts that were intimate, provocative, or even nonsensical, and it would respond without hesitation. This series is not about proving whether humans or machines are better creators. It's about what happens when we create together — when we let our imperfections and their precision collide to make something entirely new.

name: Gods Vs Gods
short_description: 2023. One work catalogued so far (15A). Title, medium, dimensions still TK.

name: Advaitha Ganesha
short_description: Inspired by my grandmother's love for Ganesha and a translation my father (D. Kalyanaraman) made of his great-grandfather's Sanskrit paper on Ganesha as Advaitha. Placeholder — no works catalogued yet.
full_description: This series is inspired by something that began as a child because of my grandmother's love for Ganesha. Ganesha is known to be the remover of obstacles and I connect very deeply with that. A lot of my life has been about turning barriers into possibilities and I was fascinated by the playfulness of Ganesha to create this series. Throughout the series I explore the philosophy of Advaitha which for me offers a framework to understand the different stages of the relationship between the true self (Atman) and the perceived other (Maya). I encountered some of these concepts when my father (D. Kalyanaraman) was working on a translation of his great-grandfather's Sanskrit paper on Ganesha as Advaitha. I use the multiple forms of Ganesha as an ode to my ancestral blessing/curse of overthinking with a child-like sense of humor and play.

name: Through the Looking Glass
short_description: A playful exploration of my eldest child Rudra at age 8 — children have a thousand faces. The looking glass as metaphor for the construction, distortion, and reconstruction of possible realities. Placeholder — no works catalogued yet.
full_description: This series was created based on a realization I had after having my 4 children that children are constantly changing. While parents are incessantly on the lookout for signs of the future in their kids, they also impose their aspirations onto them. This was the result of a playful exploration of my eldest child, Rudra, when he was 8 years old. Children have a thousand faces and that's where the beauty of accepting them at different stages lies. The looking glass in this series is used as a metaphor for the construction, distortion, and reconstruction of possible realities.

name: Anthropocene
short_description: The post-human age of the cyborg or digital native. Precursor to the thesis Karthik and I published in Critical Collective. Note: 'Anthropocene V' (work 4E) was absorbed into the Sublime Machines exhibition — flag to confirm whether this series should exist as a separate row or be folded entirely into SM.
full_description: Anthropocene is the post-human age of the cyborg or the digital native. This series was created around the time I was exploring alternative representations of transcendence relevant to our times. In this series, I explore how man creates his tools and in return they recreate him. It is an exploration of flipping these two aspects artistically of the current age of dominant human influence in the world. These works were the precursor to a thesis my brother Dr. Karthik Kalyanaraman and I wrote and published in Critical Collective called Transcendence for the Siri-ocene: or an Art for the Future.

name: Masks
short_description: Studies for the Impossible Bouquet series — performance identities, the difference between Raghava and Raghava the artist. Placeholder — no works catalogued yet.
full_description: The mask series was created at a time in my life when I was exploring performance identities within me and I realised there's a difference between Raghava and Raghava the artist. I create these different personas and notice the conflicts between them. I look for examples of other public forms of performance and show their impossible juxtapositions. These works served as studies for my series of paintings called Impossible Bouquets.

name: Ridiculous Copycats
short_description: Sequential panels that read like a graphic novel — a half-cycle of a complexity-simplicity sine wave, from species birthing to dominance to fragmentation. Placeholder — no works catalogued yet.
full_description: Ridiculous Copycats is a collection of ever increasingly complex panels of artwork that form a narrative much like a graphic novel. The narrative follows the half-cycle of a complexity-simplicity sine-wave, telling a story from the imagining/birthing of a species to its dominance over other species and ultimately other worlds. The artworks look at the origin of diversity as arising from a slight deviance or error in code — genetic, industrial, and digital. This delta, over repeated, flawed copycat attempts, births societal complexity and dominance. It is the rise of greater individual difference that fragments the original pieces until they slowly reunite again. This breath-like movement between complexity and simplicity, between group and individual, is the pulse and rhythm that ties all time, meaning, and relevance into a knot of ever-shifting identity.
